evidence.excerpt: The project investigated the relationship between seal-layer formulation variables—resin type, comonomer content, blend ratios, and film thickness—and the achievable thermal processing window on VFFS packaging lines running at up to 300 bags/min. Work was conducted across four tasks: rheological and thermal characterisation of candidate resins; cast-film extrusion trials on the laboratory line at the Faculty of Technology; heat-seal testing using a gradient sealer and a laboratory VFFS unit; and statistical modelling of composition–property relationships using RSM. The project produced seven publications and validated two target formulations with an industrial partner. A trained PhD student and two master's students were involved. Equipment procured under the project included an updated hot-tack tester and an ATR-FTIR accessory.
